namespace WhatConstant11ALeq1076GovernsTheLowerBoundOfAClosedKnotK

open MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal Topology

private abbrev E3 := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)
private abbrev E2 := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)

/-- A smooth periodic parametrization of a simple closed curve. The half-open interval is used
so that the two endpoints, which periodicity identifies, are not counted twice. -/
def IsKnotParametrization (f : ℝ → E3) : Prop :=
  ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : WithTop ℕ∞) f ∧ Function.Periodic f 1 ∧ Set.InjOn f (Set.Ico 0 1)

/-- A (tame) closed knot, represented by one smooth simple closed curve. Knot invariants below
only depend on the ambient-isotopy class of this representative. -/
structure ClosedKnot where
  parametrization : ℝ → E3
  isKnotParametrization : IsKnotParametrization parametrization

/-- Two subsets of Euclidean three-space are ambient isotopic if an isotopy of the identity
through homeomorphisms carries the first set onto the second. -/
def AmbientIsotopic (s t : Set E3) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : unitInterval → E3 ≃ₜ E3,
    Continuous (fun p : unitInterval × E3 ↦ H p.1 p.2) ∧
    H 0 = Homeomorph.refl E3 ∧ H 1 '' s = t

/-- The image of one period of a parametrized closed curve. -/
def curveImage (f : ℝ → E3) : Set E3 := f '' Set.Icc 0 1

/-- The reach of a set: the largest radius within which every point has a unique nearest point
on the set. For a positive-reach closed curve this is its knot thickness. -/
def reach (s : Set E3) : ℝ :=
  sSup {r : ℝ | 0 ≤ r ∧ ∀ p, Metric.infDist p s < r →
    ∃! x, x ∈ s ∧ dist p x = Metric.infDist p s}

/-- The length of a curve as its one-dimensional Hausdorff measure. -/
def curveLength (s : Set E3) : ℝ := (μH[1] s).toReal

/-- The ropelength of a positive-thickness curve is its length divided by its thickness. -/
def curveRopelength (s : Set E3) : ℝ := curveLength s / reach s

/-- The minimum ropelength of a knot type, expressed as the infimum over all positive-reach
embedded circles ambient isotopic to its representative. -/
def minimumRopelength (K : ClosedKnot) : ℝ :=
  sInf {r : ℝ | ∃ γ : Circle → E3,
    Topology.IsEmbedding γ ∧
    AmbientIsotopic (curveImage K.parametrization) (Set.range γ) ∧
    0 < reach (Set.range γ) ∧ r = curveRopelength (Set.range γ)}

/-- Ordered pairs of distinct parameters in one period which a planar projection identifies. -/
def crossingPairs (f : ℝ → E3) (p : E3 →L[ℝ] E2) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {q | q.1 ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 ∧ q.2 ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 ∧ q.1 ≠ q.2 ∧ p (f q.1) = p (f q.2)}

/-- A planar projection of a smooth knot parametrization is regular when it is onto, has only
finitely many crossing pairs, and the two projected tangent vectors at every crossing are
linearly independent. -/
def IsRegularProjection (f : ℝ → E3) (p : E3 →L[ℝ] E2) : Prop :=
  Function.Surjective p ∧ (crossingPairs f p).Finite ∧
    ∀ q ∈ crossingPairs f p,
      LinearIndependent ℝ (fun i : Fin 2 ↦
        if i = 0 then p (fderiv ℝ f q.1 1) else p (fderiv ℝ f q.2 1))

/-- The crossing number of a knot is the least number of crossings in a regular planar diagram.
The set `crossingPairs` uses ordered pairs, so its cardinality is divided by two. -/
def crossingNumber (K : ClosedKnot) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n : ℕ | ∃ (f : ℝ → E3) (p : E3 →L[ℝ] E2),
    IsKnotParametrization f ∧
    AmbientIsotopic (curveImage K.parametrization) (curveImage f) ∧
    IsRegularProjection f p ∧ n = (crossingPairs f p).ncard / 2}

/-- The optimal universal coefficient in the lower bound relating minimum ropelength to the
three-quarter power of crossing number. -/
def optimalLowerBoundConstant : ℝ :=
  sSup {a : ℝ | ∀ K : ClosedKnot,
    a * (crossingNumber K : ℝ) ^ (3 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ minimumRopelength K}

/-- The optimal universal constant $a$ governing
$L(K) \geq a\operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$ for every closed knot $K$ satisfies
$1.1 < a \leq 10.76$. Here $a$ is the supremum of all coefficients for which the universal
lower bound holds. -/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem what_constant_1_1_a_leq_10_76_governs_the_lower_bound_of_a_closed_knot_k :
    1.1 < optimalLowerBoundConstant ∧ optimalLowerBoundConstant ≤ 10.76 := by
  sorry

end WhatConstant11ALeq1076GovernsTheLowerBoundOfAClosedKnotK

Modeled closed knots as tame knot types represented by smooth one-periodic simple closed curves in Euclidean three-space. All invariants are then minimized over ambient-isotopic representatives, so they do not depend on the chosen representative.

Defined thickness as Federer reach—the largest radius for which nearby points have unique nearest points on the curve. The cited primary source proves that this equals knot thickness for the relevant positive-reach/C¹ curves.

Defined curve length by one-dimensional Hausdorff measure and minimum ropelength as an infimum over ambient-isotopic embedded circles of positive reach. Positive reach excludes the division-by-zero behavior that would otherwise make zero-thickness curves have Lean quotient zero.

Defined crossing number by minimizing over smooth ambient-isotopic representatives and regular surjective linear projections to the plane. Crossings are ordered pairs of distinct parameters identified by the projection; finiteness and linear independence of projected tangents enforce isolated transverse crossings, and division by two converts ordered pairs to crossings.

Included all closed knots in the universal inequality. The unknot has crossing number zero and therefore imposes no extra constraint; this matches the equivalent infimum-of-ratios formulation restricted to nontrivial knots.

Stated the combined strict lower and non-strict upper bounds as one open research theorem. This follows the fixed decomposition even though the supplied notes explain that the 10.76 upper estimate is based on computer tightening rather than a proof.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ropelength and crossing number: the constant in $L(K) \geq a \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$

The *ropelength* of a closed curve $C \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ is $\operatorname{Len}(C) / \tau(C)$,
where $\operatorname{Len}(C)$ is its length and $\tau(C)$ is its *thickness*, the radius of the
largest embedded normal tube around $C$. The (minimum) ropelength $L(K)$ of a knot type $K$ is the
infimum of the ropelength over all curves realising $K$. Buck and Simon proved that
$L(K) \geq (4\pi/11)^{3/4} \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4} \approx 1.105 \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$
for every knot $K$, where $\operatorname{Cr}(K)$ is the crossing number. Computer tightenings of
torus knots suggest that the optimal constant cannot exceed $10.76$. Wikipedia's list of unsolved
problems asks:

"What constant $1.1 < a \leq 10.76$ governs the lower bound of a closed knot $K$'s minimum
ropelength $L(K) \geq a \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$?"

Here a *knot* is a simple closed curve in $\mathbb{R}^3$, i.e. a topological embedding
`γ : Circle → ℝ³`, and two knots have the same *knot type* if their images are ambient
isotopic. Thickness is measured as a *radius* (as in Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan and
Klotz–Maldonado), which is the convention in which the constants $1.1$ and $10.76$ are stated.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Ropelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ropelength)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [BS99] Buck, G., Simon, J., *Thickness and crossing number of knots*, Topology Appl. 91 (1999),
  245–257.
- [CKS02] Cantarella, J., Kusner, R. B., Sullivan, J. M., *On the minimum ropelength of knots and
  links*, Invent. Math. 150 (2002), 257–286.
  [arXiv:math/0103224](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103224)
- [KM21] Klotz, A. R., Maldonado, M., *The ropelength of complex knots*, J. Phys. A 54 (2021).
  [arXiv:2108.01857](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.01857)
- [Kl25] Klotz, A. R., *Ropelength-minimizing concentric helices and non-alternating torus knots*.
  [arXiv:2504.00861](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00861)
-/

namespace WhatConstant11ALeq1076GovernsTheLowerBoundOfAClosedKnotK

open Topology
open scoped EuclideanGeometry MeasureTheory ENNReal Real unitInterval

/-- Two subsets `K₁ K₂` of `ℝ³` are **ambient isotopic** if there is a continuous family
`H t`, `t ∈ [0, 1]`, of homeomorphisms of `ℝ³` with `H 0 = id` and `H 1 '' K₁ = K₂`. -/
def AmbientIsotopic (K₁ K₂ : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : I → ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³, Continuous (fun p : I × ℝ³ => H p.1 p.2) ∧
    H 0 = Homeomorph.refl ℝ³ ∧ H 1 '' K₁ = K₂

/-- Every set is ambient isotopic to itself (via the constant isotopy). -/
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem AmbientIsotopic.refl (K : Set ℝ³) : AmbientIsotopic K K :=
  ⟨fun _ => Homeomorph.refl ℝ³, continuous_snd, rfl, by simp⟩

/-- The **thickness** of a set `K ⊆ ℝ³`, following Gonzalez–Maddocks and [CKS02, §1]: the
infimum of the circumradii $r(x, y, z)$ over all triples of distinct points $x, y, z \in K$.
Collinear triples have $r = \infty$ and are omitted (they never contribute to the infimum). For a
`C¹` curve this equals the normal injectivity radius, i.e. the radius of the largest embedded
normal tube around the curve [CKS02, §1]; it is `0` for curves that are not `C^{1,1}`. -/
noncomputable def thickness (K : Set ℝ³) : ℝ :=
  sInf {r | ∃ s : Affine.Simplex ℝ ℝ³ 2, (∀ i, s.points i ∈ K) ∧ s.circumradius = r}

/-- The **ropelength** of a set `K ⊆ ℝ³` (the image of a closed curve): its length, i.e. its
one-dimensional Hausdorff measure `μH[1] K`, divided by its thickness. It is `∞` when the curve
has zero thickness (and positive length) or infinite length. -/
noncomputable def ropelength (K : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  μH[1] K / ENNReal.ofReal (thickness K)

/-- The **minimum ropelength** of the knot type of the knot `γ`: the infimum of the ropelength
over all knots `γ'` whose image is ambient isotopic to that of `γ`. -/
noncomputable def minRopelength (γ : Circle → ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (γ' : Circle → ℝ³)
    (_ : IsEmbedding γ' ∧ AmbientIsotopic (Set.range γ) (Set.range γ')),
    ropelength (Set.range γ')

/-- The vertical projection `ℝ³ → ℝ × ℝ` onto the first two coordinates. -/
def planeProj (p : ℝ³) : ℝ × ℝ := (p 0, p 1)

/-- The `2π`-periodic parametrisation `t ↦ γ (Circle.exp t)` of a curve
`γ : Circle → ℝ³`. -/
noncomputable def periodicParam (γ : Circle → ℝ³) : ℝ → ℝ³ :=
  fun t => γ (Circle.exp t)

/-- The **crossings** of the vertical projection of `γ : Circle → ℝ³`: the points of the plane
with exactly two preimages on the curve. -/
def crossingSet (γ : Circle → ℝ³) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {p | (Set.range γ ∩ planeProj ⁻¹' {p}).encard = 2}

/-- The curve `γ : Circle → ℝ³` is `C¹` and its vertical projection to the plane is a
**regular diagram**: the projected curve is an immersion, every point of the plane has at most
two preimages on the curve, there are finitely many double points, and at every double point
the two strands cross transversally. -/
structure IsRegularDiagram (γ : Circle → ℝ³) : Prop where
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ 1 (periodicParam γ)
  immersion : ∀ t, deriv (planeProj ∘ periodicParam γ) t ≠ 0
  encard_le_two : ∀ p, (Set.range γ ∩ planeProj ⁻¹' {p}).encard ≤ 2
  finite : (crossingSet γ).Finite
  transverse : ∀ t₁ t₂, periodicParam γ t₁ ≠ periodicParam γ t₂ →
    planeProj (periodicParam γ t₁) = planeProj (periodicParam γ t₂) →
    LinearIndependent ℝ
      ![deriv (planeProj ∘ periodicParam γ) t₁, deriv (planeProj ∘ periodicParam γ) t₂]

/-- The **crossing number** of the knot type of the knot `γ`: the least number of crossings in a
regular diagram of a knot `γ'` whose image is ambient isotopic to that of `γ`. (Any regular
projection direction can be rotated to the vertical one by an ambient isotopy, so it suffices to
consider vertical projections.) For a knot type with no `C¹` representative (a wild knot) the set
below is empty and the value is `0`; such knot types have infinite ropelength. -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (γ : Circle → ℝ³) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ γ' : Circle → ℝ³,
    IsEmbedding γ' ∧ AmbientIsotopic (Set.range γ) (Set.range γ') ∧
    IsRegularDiagram γ' ∧ (crossingSet γ').ncard = n}

/-- The optimal constant `a` in the lower bound $L(K) \geq a \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$: the
supremum of all `a : ℝ` such that `a * Cr(K) ^ (3/4) ≤ L(K)` holds for every knot type `K`,
where `L(K)` is the minimum ropelength and `Cr(K)` the crossing number of `K`. -/
noncomputable def ropelengthCrossingConstant : ℝ :=
  sSup {a : ℝ | ∀ γ : Circle → ℝ³, IsEmbedding γ →
    ENNReal.ofReal (a * (crossingNumber γ : ℝ) ^ (3 / 4 : ℝ)) ≤ minRopelength γ}

/--
**Ropelength versus crossing number.**
Let $a^*$ be the optimal constant such that every closed knot $K$ satisfies
$L(K) \geq a^* \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$, where $L(K)$ is the minimum ropelength and
$\operatorname{Cr}(K)$ the crossing number of $K$. Then $1.1 < a^* \leq 10.76$.

The lower bound is the theorem of Buck and Simon [BS99] (see also [CKS02, §5]), which gives
$a^* \geq (4\pi/11)^{3/4} \approx 1.105$. The upper bound rests on computer tightenings of
$T(Q+1, Q)$ torus knots with at least $224$ crossings [KM21], [Kl25], and is not proven.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 57]
theorem what_constant_1_1_a_leq_10_76_governs_the_lower_bound_of_a_closed_knot_k :
    1.1 < ropelengthCrossingConstant ∧ ropelengthCrossingConstant ≤ 10.76 := by
  sorry

/-- The lower half: the optimal constant exceeds $1.1$. This follows from the theorem of
Buck and Simon [BS99], since $(4\pi/11)^{3/4} > 1.1$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 51 57]
theorem what_constant_1_1_a_leq_10_76_governs_the_lower_bound_of_a_closed_knot_k.variants.lower_bound :
    1.1 < ropelengthCrossingConstant := by
  sorry

/-- The theorem of Buck and Simon [BS99], as stated in [CKS02, §5]: every knot type $K$ satisfies
$L(K) \geq (4\pi \operatorname{Cr}(K) / 11)^{3/4}$; hence $a^* \geq (4\pi/11)^{3/4}$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 51 57]
theorem what_constant_1_1_a_leq_10_76_governs_the_lower_bound_of_a_closed_knot_k.variants.buck_simon :
    (4 * π / 11) ^ (3 / 4 : ℝ) ≤ ropelengthCrossingConstant := by
  sorry

/-- The upper half: the optimal constant is at most $10.76$, i.e. there are knots $K$ whose
minimum ropelength is arbitrarily close to (or below) $10.76 \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$. This is
supported by computer tightenings of torus knots [KM21], [Kl25], but is not proven. -/
@[category research open, AMS 51 57]
theorem what_constant_1_1_a_leq_10_76_governs_the_lower_bound_of_a_closed_knot_k.variants.upper_bound :
    ropelengthCrossingConstant ≤ 10.76 := by
  sorry

/-- The question in its literal form: what is the optimal constant $a^*$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 51 57]
theorem what_constant_1_1_a_leq_10_76_governs_the_lower_bound_of_a_closed_knot_k.variants.value :
    ropelengthCrossingConstant = answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

end WhatConstant11ALeq1076GovernsTheLowerBoundOfAClosedKnotK

The table's reading (a* = sup of valid constants, single Prop 1.1 < a* ∧ a* ≤ 10.76, knots only, radius convention implied by the cited constants) was followed; the suggested split into a proven lower half and an unproven upper half was implemented as additional variant declarations with categories research solved / research open respectively, while the slot declaration itself carries the conjunction with category research open.
modeling_decisions: Convention: thickness is the RADIUS of the largest embedded normal tube (Gonzalez–Maddocks / Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan / Klotz–Maldonado convention). This is the convention in which both constants of the statement live: (4π/11)^{3/4} ≈ 1.105 (CKS §5 citing Buck–Simon, radius convention) and 10.76 (Klotz–Maldonado, unit-radius tubes). Note the Wikipedia article's other numbers (15.66, 16.372) are in the diameter convention; in that convention the constants would be halved.

The unknown constant a* is defined as sSup {a : ℝ | ∀ knot γ, ofReal(a·Cr(γ)^{3/4}) ≤ minRopelength γ}. This set contains all a ≤ 0 and is bounded above (any smooth trefoil has finite ropelength and Cr = 3), so sSup is the genuine supremum; it equals the infimum of L(K)/Cr(K)^{3/4} over nontrivial knots (the unknot, Cr = 0, imposes no constraint), matching the decomposition note.

Knots are topological embeddings γ : Circle → ℝ³ (as in Wikipedia/InscribedSquare.lean); knot type = ambient isotopy of the image sets, via a continuous family H : I → (ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³) with H 0 = id and H 1 '' K₁ = K₂. # The constant relating ropelength and crossing number

The *ropelength* of a closed curve $C$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is $\operatorname{Len}(C) / \tau(C)$,
where $\operatorname{Len}(C)$ is its length and $\tau(C)$ is its *thickness*, the radius of the
largest embedded normal tube around $C$. Following Gonzalez–Maddocks and
Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan, the thickness is the infimum, over all triples of distinct points of
$C$, of the radius of the circle through them. The (minimum) ropelength $L(K)$ of a knot type $K$
is the infimum of the ropelength over all curves realising $K$. We write $\operatorname{Cr}(K)$
for the crossing number of $K$: the least number of crossings in a regular projection of a
curve realising $K$.

Buck and Simon proved that there is a constant $a > 0$ such that every knot $K$ satisfies
$L(K) \geq a \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$; their constant is $(4\pi/11)^{3/4} \approx 1.105$.
Computer tightenings of $T(Q+1, Q)$ torus knots with at least $224$ crossings give knots with
$L(K) / \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4} \approx 10.76$. The optimal constant is unknown:

> What constant $1.1 < a \leq 10.76$ governs the lower bound of a closed knot $K$'s minimum
> ropelength $L(K) \geq a\operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$?

Ropelength is measured in units of the tube *radius* (so that the trefoil has ropelength
approximately $32.74$), which is the convention in which the constants $1.1$ and $10.76$ are
stated.

 - [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)

 - [Wikipedia, Crossing number (knot theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossing_number_(knot_theory))

 - J. Cantarella, R. B. Kusner, J. M. Sullivan, *On the minimum ropelength of knots and links*,

 - A. Klotz, F. Thompson, *Ropelength-minimizing concentric helices and non-alternating torus

namespace WhatConstant11ALeq1076GovernsTheLowerBoundOfAClosedKnotK

/-- A knot, given as a closed curve `γ : ℝ → ℝ³` of period `1` that is injective on a
period, continuously differentiable and regular (nowhere vanishing derivative). Every such curve
is a tame knot, and every tame knot type contains such a curve. -/
structure IsKnot (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Prop where
  periodic : Function.Periodic γ 1
  injOn : Set.InjOn γ (Set.Ico 0 1)
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ 1 γ
  deriv_ne_zero : ∀ t, deriv γ t ≠ 0

/-- Two subsets `K₁ K₂` of `ℝ³` are *ambient isotopic* if there is a continuous family
`H t` (`t ∈ [0, 1]`) of homeomorphisms of `ℝ³`, with `H 0` the identity, such that `H 1`
maps `K₁` onto `K₂`. Two knots have the same knot type when their images are ambient
isotopic. -/
def AmbientIsotopic (K₁ K₂ : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : I → ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³, Continuous (fun p : I × ℝ³ => H p.1 p.2) ∧
    H 0 = Homeomorph.refl ℝ³ ∧ H 1 '' K₁ = K₂

open scoped Classical in
/-- The radius of the circle through three points of `ℝ³`, taken to be `∞` when the points
are collinear (in particular when two of them coincide). -/
noncomputable def tripleCircumradius (x y z : ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  if h : AffineIndependent ℝ ![x, y, z] then
    ENNReal.ofReal (⟨![x, y, z], h⟩ : Affine.Triangle ℝ ℝ³).circumradius
  else ⊤

/-- The *thickness* of a set `K ⊆ ℝ³` (in the sense of Gonzalez–Maddocks and
Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan): the infimum over all triples of distinct points of `K` of the
radius of the circle through them. For a `C¹` closed curve this is the radius of the largest
embedded normal tube around the curve (its reach). -/
noncomputable def thickness (K : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (x ∈ K) (y ∈ K) (z ∈ K) (_ : x ≠ y) (_ : x ≠ z) (_ : y ≠ z),
    tripleCircumradius x y z

/-- The *ropelength* of the knot type of a knot `γ₀`: the infimum, over all knots `γ` ambient
isotopic to `γ₀`, of the length of `γ` divided by the thickness of its image. -/
noncomputable def ropelength (γ₀ : ℝ → ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) (_ : IsKnot γ) (_ : AmbientIsotopic (Set.range γ₀) (Set.range γ)),
    eVariationOn γ (Set.Icc 0 1) / thickness (Set.range γ)

/-- The *crossings* of the projection of the curve `γ` along the linear map `p : ℝ³ → ℝ²`:
the points of the plane that are the image of at least two distinct points of the curve. -/
def crossings (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) (p : ℝ³ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ²) : Set ℝ² :=
  {q | ∃ x ∈ Set.range γ, ∃ y ∈ Set.range γ, x ≠ y ∧ p x = q ∧ p y = q}

/-- The linear map `p : ℝ³ → ℝ²` is a *regular projection* of the knot `γ` if it is a
projection onto a plane (surjective), the projected curve `p ∘ γ` is an immersion, and it has
only finitely many multiple points, each of which is a transverse double point. -/
structure IsRegularProjection (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) (p : ℝ³ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ²) : Prop where
  surjective : Function.Surjective p
  immersion : ∀ t, p (deriv γ t) ≠ 0
  finite : (crossings γ p).Finite
  no_triple : ∀ x ∈ Set.range γ, ∀ y ∈ Set.range γ, ∀ z ∈ Set.range γ,
    x ≠ y → x ≠ z → y ≠ z → p x = p y → p y ≠ p z
  transverse : ∀ s t : ℝ, γ s ≠ γ t → p (γ s) = p (γ t) →
    LinearIndependent ℝ ![p (deriv γ s), p (deriv γ t)]

/-- The *crossing number* of the knot type of a knot `γ₀`: the least number of crossings of a
regular projection of a knot ambient isotopic to `γ₀`. -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (γ₀ : ℝ → ℝ³) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ γ, IsKnot γ ∧ AmbientIsotopic (Set.range γ₀) (Set.range γ) ∧
    ∃ p : ℝ³ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ², IsRegularProjection γ p ∧ (crossings γ p).ncard = n}

/-- The optimal constant `a` in the lower bound $L(K) \geq a \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$: the
supremum of all real `a` such that every knot `K` satisfies
$L(K) \geq a \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$. Equivalently, the infimum of
$L(K) / \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$ over all nontrivial knots `K`. -/
noncomputable def ropelengthCrossingConstant : ℝ :=
  sSup {a : ℝ | ∀ γ, IsKnot γ →
    ENNReal.ofReal (a * (crossingNumber γ : ℝ) ^ (3 / 4 : ℝ)) ≤ ropelength γ}

/-- Ambient isotopy is reflexive: the constant family of identity homeomorphisms is an
ambient isotopy from any set to itself. -/
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem AmbientIsotopic.refl (K : Set ℝ³) : AmbientIsotopic K K :=
  ⟨fun _ => Homeomorph.refl ℝ³, continuous_snd, rfl, Set.image_id K⟩

-/

    1.1 < ropelengthCrossingConstant ∧ ropelengthCrossingConstant ≤ 10.76 := by

the quotient of its length by its *thickness* $\tau(C)$, the radius of the largest embedded normal
tube around $C$. Following Gonzalez–Maddocks and Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan, $\tau(C)$ is the

$K$, where $\operatorname{Cr}(K)$ is the crossing number, and $(4\pi/11)^{3/4} \approx 1.105$.

$L(K) \leq 10.76 \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$. The optimal constant $a$ is unknown.

Ropelength = Len/τ in these units, which is the normalisation in which Buck–Simon's bound is (4π/11)^{3/4} ≈ 1.105 and Klotz–Maldonado's tightened torus knots give 10.76; in diameter units both numbers would be halved.

Length of a curve is taken to be its one-dimensional Hausdorff measure μH[1] of the image set (equal to arclength for simple curves; Mathlib normalises μH[1] = Lebesgue on ℝ). This lets everything be set-based.

Ropelength is ℝ≥0∞-valued: `μH[1] K / ENNReal.ofReal (thickness K)`. With ENNReal conventions a curve of zero thickness (e.g. polygonal or wild) or infinite length gets ropelength ⊤, matching the literature (L(K)=∞ for wild knots) and avoiding Lean's x/0 = 0 junk.

Knots are subsets of ℝ³ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) that are images of topological embeddings of `Circle`; knot type is ambient isotopy: a jointly continuous family H : [0,1] → (ℝ³ → ℝ³) of homeomorphisms with H 0 = id and H 1 '' K = K'. Minimum ropelength L(K) is the ⨅ of ropelength over all sets ambient isotopic to K (which includes K itself). Tameness is not imposed: wild knots have L = ⊤ and hence impose no constraint on a, exactly as in the informal statement.

Crossing number: sInf over all K' ambient isotopic to K and all surjective linear maps P : ℝ³ → ℝ² such that every fibre meets K' in ≤ 2 points and the set of fibres meeting K' in exactly 2 points is finite, of the number of such fibres. Transversality of the double points is not required; this does not change the minimum (a non-transverse double point can be removed or converted to a genuine crossing by an ambient isotopy, and any planar embedded finite graph is tame), so for tame knots this equals the standard crossing number. For a wild knot the set is empty and `sInf ∅ = 0` in ℕ, but this is harmless because L(K) = ⊤ there.

The unknot has Cr = 0, so 0 ≤ L(K) constrains nothing; hence no explicit 'nontrivial' hypothesis is needed and the constant is the sSup of {a | ∀ knots K, ofReal(a·Cr(K)^{3/4}) ≤ L(K)}. This set contains 0 and is bounded above (e.g. by L(trefoil)/3^{3/4}), so the real sSup is the genuine optimal constant a*.

The bounds are 1.1 < a* (strict) and a* ≤ 10.76 (non-strict), as in the statement. Following the decomposition notes, the proven half (Buck–Simon, also stated explicitly as `(4π/11 · Cr(K))^{3/4} ≤ L(K)`) is tagged research solved and the numerical half (a* ≤ 10.76) research open; the slot declaration itself is the conjunction, tagged research open.
AMS tags 53 (differential geometry, curves in ℝ³) and 57 (manifolds; knot theory) are used.
The 'what constant' question itself is not formalised with `answer(sorry)`, per the task's Dropped list.

modeling_decisions: The decomposition identifies a* as the optimal universal constant, equivalently the infimum of L(K) / Cr(K)^(3/4) over nontrivial closed knot types; this is the intended reading of the terse list-page question.

The domain must be nontrivial knots: including the unknot gives crossing number zero and makes the ratio formulation degenerate, while the universal-inequality formulation does not let the unknot determine the optimal constant.
The 10.76 upper estimate is specific to knots (not links), consistent with both the decomposition and the cited torus-knot computations.

what_constant_1_1_a_leq_10_76_governs_th.why: A faithful statement requires a type of tame closed knot types (ambient-isotopy classes of embedded circles in Euclidean 3-space), minimum ropelength defined by minimizing curve length divided by knot thickness/reach within each knot type, crossing number defined by minimizing crossings over regular diagrams/projections, and the resulting infimum over nontrivial knot types. Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib provide generic topological embeddings and bounded variation, but no knot types or ambient isotopy, knot thickness/reach/embedded normal tubes, regular knot diagrams, or knot crossing number. Introducing arbitrary abstract functions for L(K) and Cr(K) would not constrain them to the geometric invariants in the source and would therefore state a model-dependent, potentially vacuous proposition rather than the conjecture. Building all missing notions faithfully would require a substantial knot/curve geometry theory rather than a small bespoke definition.
